H8098N.emploi: Schemaeja appears only once in the Bible, in Ezra 8:13. He is mentioned among the sons or descendants of Adonikam who returned with Ezra from Babylon around 458 B.C. This brief mention places him in the context of the return of the exiles and the restoration of Jerusalem after the destruction of the temple. His inclusion in these genealogical lists shows that he was a head of household or a notable significant enough to be named.

sens: name of a Levite who returned from exile with Ezra
H8098O.detail: Schemaeja is a Levite mentioned only once in the Bible, in Ezra 8:16, among the leaders whom the prophet Ezra summoned for an important message regarding the return from exile to Jerusalem. His name appears in the list of men called to participate in the organization of the return of the exiles and the restoration of worship.
H8098O.origine: The Hebrew name Schemaeja (שְׁמַעְיָהוּ) literally means "Heard by the Lord" or "God has listened" — composed of "shamea" (heard) and "Yah" (the Lord). It is a theophoric name, like many Hebrew names, expressing confidence in divine intervention. Several individuals bear this name in the Old Testament, at different periods in the history of Israel.
H8098O.emploi: Schemaeja appears only once in the Segond 1910 translation — in Ezra 8:16. He is presented as one of the leaders gathered by Ezra before the return journey from Babylon. The context indicates that Ezra summoned him to receive an important mission related to the organization of the return from exile and the resettlement of the people in Jerusalem. His exact role is not detailed, but his presence among the "leaders" shows that he held a position of responsibility among the Levites.

sens: Member of the family of Harim who had taken a foreign wife at the time of Ezra
H8098P.detail: Schemaeja is one of the Israelites from the family of Harim mentioned in Ezra 10:21 among those who had married foreign women and who, at Ezra's command, had to repudiate them upon the return from Babylonian exile. This name appears in the list of measures for religious and moral restoration of the restored Jewish community.
H8098P.origine: The name Schemaeja literally means "Heard by Jehovah" or "God has heard," composed of the Hebrew "shama" (to hear) and the divine "Yah." It is a typical theophoric name, expressing the confidence that the Lord hears the prayer of the one who bears this name. Several biblical characters bear this name at different periods in the history of Israel.
H8098P.emploi: Schemaeja is mentioned only once in the Bible, in Ezra 10:21. He is listed among the sons of Harim who, upon the return from exile, had contracted marriages with women from surrounding peoples, which was considered a violation of the law and a threat to the religious purity of Israel. Like the others named in this list, he had to separate from his foreign wife.

sens: Israelite of the lineage of Harim who had married a foreign woman at the time of Ezra
H8098Q.detail: 1. Schemaeja is a man of the people of Israel, a member of the clan of Harim, who lived at the time of the return from Babylonian exile under Ezra's leadership. Among the Israelites who returned to Jerusalem, several had married foreign women, which was forbidden by the Law; Schemaeja is one such example (Ezra 10:31).
H8098Q.origine: The name Schemaeja literally means "Heard by Jehovah": it comes from two Hebrew words, "Shema" (to hear) and "Yah" (God). It was a common name among the Israelites, borne by many individuals in biblical history — prophets, Levites, priests — but this Schemaeja of the lineage of Harim is known only by this unique mention in Ezra.
H8098Q.emploi: Schemaeja is mentioned only once in the Bible, in Ezra 10:31. At that time, Ezra discovered that members of the people, including priests, had married women from neighboring and idolatrous peoples. This was considered a serious violation of the covenant and the purity of God's people. Ezra gathered all those who had committed this offense and urged them to repudiate these foreign women. Schemaeja is included in this list of men who repented and obeyed this command.
H8098Q.portee: This passage shows us the importance that the Bible places on faithfulness to the Lord and separation from what may draw us away from Him. Schemaeja represents the people called to repent and turn back to God after the exile. His name, which means "Heard by Jehovah," suggests that God hears the cry of His people returning to Him.

sens: Man of Judah, son of Schecaniah, who worked on the reconstruction of the wall of Jerusalem under Nehemiah
H8098R.detail: Schemaeja is a man of the people of Judah mentioned only once in the Bible, in Nehemiah 3:29, where he is presented as the son of Schecaniah and the keeper of the East Gate. His name means "Heard by the Lord." He actively participates in the reconstruction of the wall of Jerusalem after the return from exile, a crucial work of restoration for the Jewish community.
H8098R.origine: The name Schemaeja comes from the Hebrew שׁמע (shamá, "to hear") and יה (yah, abbreviation of the divine name Jehovah). It literally means "Heard by the Lord" or "the Lord has heard." It is a common name in Israel, borne by several different men during the periods of the monarchy, exile, and return.
H8098R.emploi: Schemaeja appears only once in the Bible, in Nehemiah 3:29, during the reconstruction of the wall of Jerusalem under Nehemiah's leadership (circa 445 B.C.). He is presented as the son of Schecaniah and the keeper of the East Gate. His role is modest but significant: he participates in the building of this wall, a symbol of the restoration of Jerusalem and the revival of the worship of the True God after the Babylonian exile. His work is part of the collective project of reconstruction to which the entire community contributes.
H8098R.portee: The mention of Schemaeja, although brief, reminds us that the restoration of Jerusalem was not the work of a single man, but of an entire community. Even the anonymous or lesser-known figures had their place in God's plan. This teaches that in the building of God's kingdom, everyone has a role to play, whether visible or hidden.

sens: A man from the time of the return from exile, son of Delaiah
Son of Mehetabel, a false prophet hired by Tobiah and Sanballat to deceive Nehemiah
H8098S.detail: 1. Schemaeja is a character mentioned only once in the Bible, in Nehemiah 6:10, during the reconstruction of the walls of Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. His name means "heard by the Lord." 2. He is a false prophet, son of Delaiah and grandson of Mehetabel, who was paid to give bad advice to Nehemiah. In Nehemiah 6:10, he locks himself in the temple and asks Nehemiah to come hide there, claiming that men are coming to kill him at night — advice intended to frighten and divert Nehemiah from his work.
H8098S.origine: The Hebrew name שְׁמַעְיָהוּ (Shemaiah) comes from שׁמע (shamá), which means "to hear" or "to listen," and from יָהּ (Yah), the abbreviation of the divine name Yahweh. Its meaning is therefore "heard by the Lord" or "the Lord has heard." It is a common name in Israel — the Bible mentions more than twenty different bearers — expressing the confidence that God hears the prayers of His people.
H8098S.emploi: Schemaeja is a minor character in the Bible, mentioned only once in Nehemiah 6:10. He represents one of the many tactics used by Nehemiah's enemies to stop him from rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem upon the return from exile. He is a false prophet who was paid to frighten him with false prophecies of death, pushing him to take refuge in the temple — an act that would have discredited him before the people. His role in the narrative shows how the opponents of the reconstruction project sought to exploit fear and religious superstition to hinder God's work.

sens: Priest during the time of Nehemiah
H8098T.detail: Schemaeja is a priest who lived at the time of the return from exile, under the reign of Nehemiah. His name literally means "heard by the Lord" in Hebrew. He appears in the lists of those who sealed the renewed covenant with God (Nehemiah 10:8), among the priests who solemnly committed to observe the Law. He is also mentioned during the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem (Nehemiah 12:6, 12:18, 12:34), a major event that celebrated the restoration of the city and marked the spiritual renewal of the people after the exile. Schemaeja thus represents one of the clergy figures who actively participated in the religious and civil reconstruction of the community of Judah.
H8098T.origine: The name Schemaeja comes from the Hebrew שְׁמַעְיָהוּ (shemaiah), composed of two elements: שׁמע (shamaʿ, "to hear, to listen") and יָה (Yah, the shortened divine name meaning "Lord"). The name therefore means "heard by the Lord" or "listened to by the Lord," expressing the idea that God listens to and hears the one who bears this name. This type of theophoric name (containing the name of God) was common in Israel and reflected confidence in divine listening. Several characters bear this name in the Old Testament, including a prophet during the time of Rehoboam and a false prophet during the time of Jeremiah, but this one is specifically a priest from the return from exile.
H8098T.emploi: Schemaeja is mentioned four times in the book of Nehemiah, always during the reconstruction period that followed the return from the Babylonian exile. In Nehemiah 10:8, he is among the priests who signed the solemn covenant committing the people to respect the Law of Moses — a fundamental act in the religious restoration of Jerusalem. Later, in Nehemiah 12:6 and 12:18, his name appears in the genealogy of the priests, highlighting his role in organizing the worship of the Second Temple. Finally, in Nehemiah 12:34, he is cited as one of the spiritual leaders present at the dedication of the rebuilt wall of Jerusalem, a festive and solemn event that confirmed the complete restoration of the holy city. These four occurrences consistently present him in a context of commitment to God and participation in the major religious ceremonies of his time.

sens: A man of the tribe of Judah during the Exile and the Return
H8098U.detail: Schemaeja is a proper name designating a man of Judah mentioned only once in the Bible, in Nehemiah 12:35. He is the father of Jonathan and the son of Mattaniah, placing him in a genealogy of priests involved in the restoration of worship in Jerusalem after the Exile. His name means "heard by the Lord" and expresses the conviction that God listens to those who cry out to Him. Although few details are given about his personal life, his presence in this genealogy shows that he belonged to a family of ministers of worship, important actors in the religious renewal of Judah during the return from the Exile.
H8098U.origine: The name Schemaeja comes from the Hebrew שְׁמַע ("to listen") and יָה ("Jah," the Lord). It belongs to a family of common theophoric names in the Bible, where the name expresses a relationship with God: "heard by the Lord." This structure reminds us that God hears the prayers and cries of His people.
H8098U.emploi: Schemaeja is mentioned only once in the provided biblical usages, in Nehemiah 12:35, where he is cited in a genealogical list of priests who played the trumpet during the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem after the Return from Exile. He is presented as the son of Mattaniah and the father of Jonathan, an ancestor of the priest Zechariah. This brief mention places him in the history of the restoration of the temple and worship in Jerusalem under Nehemiah's leadership.

sens: Levitical musician during the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah
H8098V.detail: Schemaeja is a Levite who participates in the solemn celebration of the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, rebuilt after the exile. He is part of a group of Levitical musicians who accompany this important ceremony with musical instruments, as reported in Nehemiah 12:36. His name means "heard by the Lord," which is fitting for a servant of the temple engaged in public worship.
H8098V.origine: The name Schemaeja is composed of two Hebrew elements: "Shema" (to hear) and "Yah" (abbreviation of the Lord). It literally means "heard by the Lord" or "the Lord has heard." It is a common theophoric name in Israel, expressing the confidence that God listens to the prayers of His people. Several characters bear this name in the Old Testament, but this one is specifically the Levitical musician from the time of Nehemiah.
H8098V.emploi: Schemaeja is mentioned only once in the Bible, in Nehemiah 12:36. He is presented as one of the Levitical brothers—probably musicians or singers—who participate in the grand procession of dedication of the wall of Jerusalem. This moment is an act of recognition towards God after the return from exile to Babylon. Schemaeja and his Levitical companions play a central liturgical role in animating this public celebration with the traditional musical instruments of the temple.
H8098V.portee: This brief account of the dedication of the wall shows how the people returned from exile strive to restore the worship of the Lord and rebuild their community. Schemaeja, as a Levitical musician, represents those who dedicate their service to public worship, reminding us that praise and music have always held an honored place in the worship of Israel.

sens: Character mentioned in the account of the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem during the time of Nehemiah
H8098W.detail: Schemaeja is a Levite mentioned only once in the Bible, during the ceremony of dedicating the wall of Jerusalem rebuilt after the exile to Babylon. He is among the singers and musicians who participated in this solemn celebration (Nehemiah 12:42), alongside several other Levites including Maaseiah, Eleazar, and Johanan. His role in this passage is to be a witness and participant in this important moment of restoration for the Jewish people returning from exile.
H8098W.origine: The name Schemaeja means "heard by the Lord" in Hebrew (from "Shema," to hear, and "Yah," Lord). It is a typical theophoric name of the people of Israel, expressing the confidence that the Lord hears the prayers of His people. Several characters bore this name in biblical history, but this one is specifically a Levite from the time of Nehemiah.
H8098W.emploi: Schemaeja appears only once in the Scriptures, in Nehemiah 12:42, during the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem. He is presented as a singing Levite among the musical group that celebrated the restoration of the holy city after the return from exile. His appearance in this festive and liturgical context shows the importance of the role of the Levites in the renewed worship of the restored people. Although little known, Schemaeja represents the many unnamed servants who contributed to the reconstruction of the Israelite community.

sens: father of the prophet Uriah, from Kirjath-Jearim, during the time of Jeremiah
H8098X.detail: Schemaeja is a man whose name is mentioned only once in the Bible, as the father of Uriah. Uriah was a prophet who lived in Kirjath-Jearim and who, like Jeremiah, prophesied against Jerusalem and Judah in the name of the Lord (Jeremiah 26:20). Although Schemaeja himself does not appear in the biblical accounts, his son Uriah is presented as an important prophetic figure during the time of Jeremiah, suggesting that Schemaeja was a man of faith in a family of servants of God.
H8098X.origine: The name Schemaeja means "heard by the Lord" or "the Lord has heard." It is formed from the Hebrew "Shéma" (to hear, to listen) and "Yahu" (abbreviation of the divine name Yahweh). It is a common theophoric name in Israel, expressing the confidence that the Lord listens to the prayers and cries of His people. Several other biblical characters bear this same name at different periods in the history of Israel.
H8098X.emploi: Schemaeja appears only once in the Bible, in Jeremiah 26:20, where he is presented as the father of Uriah, a prophet of the Lord from Kirjath-Jearim. Uriah is mentioned in the context of the controversy surrounding Jeremiah: he prophesied the same words as Jeremiah against Jerusalem and against the land of Judah. This unique mention shows us that Schemaeja was the father of a prophet faithful to the Lord during the troubled days of the reign of Jehoiakim, king of Judah. The text tells us nothing more about Schemaeja himself, but his presence in the biblical narrative honors the prophetic lineage from which Uriah came.

sens: A false prophet during the time of Jeremiah
H8098Y.detail: Schemaeja is one of the many characters called this in the Hebrew Bible. The one mentioned here is described as a "Nehelamite" (from a locality or clan called Nehelam) and lives during the time of the prophet Jeremiah, during the exile to Babylon. He is a false prophet: he predicted to the Israelite captives that their deportation would end quickly, while God had not sent him for that purpose. In Jeremiah 29:31-32, the Lord declares that He will punish him and his descendants, for his words are a rebellion against God.
H8098Y.origine: The Hebrew name Shemaiah literally means "heard by the Lord" or "the Lord has heard." It comes from the root "shama" (to hear) and the divine name "Yah." It was a common theophoric name in Israel, borne by at least thirty different characters in the Scriptures. The same name also designates a faithful prophet during the time of Rehoboam (1 Kings 12:22) and various other figures, including Levites and priests.
H8098Y.emploi: Schemaeja the Nehelamite appears only in Jeremiah 29:24-32. This is a short pericope in which Jeremiah reports a message from the Lord addressed to the exiles in Babylon. Schemaeja circulated letters among the captives, encouraging them to rebel against Jeremiah and against the message of the Lord, which announced that the exile would last seventy years (Jeremiah 29:10). In contrast, Schemaeja promised a quick return, thus giving a "false confidence" to the people. He embodied the category of false prophets that Jeremiah criticizes throughout his ministry.
H8098Y.portee: The story of Schemaeja warns us of the danger of false prophets who reassure the people with lies, instead of faithfully conveying the word of God. It shows that the criterion of a true prophet is not popularity or the comfort he brings, but his sending by God and the conformity of his message to divine will. For the believer today, this invites discernment of spiritual voices with vigilance, in light of Scripture.

sens: father of Deliah, a prince of Judah during the time of the prophet Jeremiah
H8098Z.detail: Schemaeja is a character from the Old Testament, mentioned only once in the Bible: he is the father of Deliah, who is among the leaders of Judah during the time of the prophet Jeremiah. Deliah was significant enough to sit in the royal secretary's chamber during the reading of the prophet's scroll, indicating that Schemaeja himself belonged to a high-ranking family.
H8098Z.origine: The name Schemaeja means "heard by Jehovah": it combines the idea of being listened to or heard with the divine name. It is a typical theophoric name from the royal period, expressing the confidence that the Lord hears the prayers and cries of His people.
H8098Z.emploi: Schemaeja appears only once in the Bible, in Jeremiah 36:12. He is identified there as the father of Deliah, one of the princes who listened to the reading of the prophetic scroll of the prophet Jeremiah. His existence confirms the importance of certain noble families in Jerusalem during this troubled period, just before the fall of the city.

sens: Members of the tribe of Israel descended from Simeon
Descendants of the patriarch Simeon, son of Jacob and Leah
Inhabitants or warriors of the territory assigned to the tribe of Simeon
H8099.detail:
1. The Simeonites are the members of the people of Israel who descend from Simeon, one of the twelve sons of the patriarch Jacob (Israel) and his first wife Leah. Simeon was born in Paddan-Aram and became the father of six sons: Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zerah, and Shaul (Genesis 46:10).
2. At the time of the census of the people in the desert, the Simeonites formed a tribe organized into families, led by recognized leaders. The number of men registered "twenty years old and above, able to go to war" was twenty-two thousand two hundred (Numbers 26:14), making them one of the tribes of Israel.
3. During the division of the promised land, the Simeonites received a territory enclosed within the lands of Judah (Joshua 21:4-7), reflecting a particular position in the organization of the kingdom of Israel. Their military leaders and families are listed alongside those of the other tribes (1 Chronicles 27:16).
H8099.origine: The name Simeonites (in Hebrew Shimoni or Shim'oni) derives from Simeon (Shimeon), whose name means "God has heard" — Leah said at the birth of her son: "The Lord has heard that I am unloved; He has given me this one also" (Genesis 29:33). The formation of the word Simeonites follows the usual Hebrew pattern for designating members of a tribe or descendants of an eponymous ancestor.
H8099.emploi: The term Simeonites appears four times in the Segond 1910 translations, always to designate the organized members of this tribe during the periods of the desert and the settlement in Canaan. It is used to enumerate them in the official censuses (Numbers 25:14 and 26:14), to assign the Levitical cities to the tribe (Joshua 21:4), and to list their military leaders during the time of King David (1 Chronicles 27:16). These contexts show that the Simeonites maintain an organized and recognized tribal identity even after settling in Canaan.
H8099.portee: The people of God at Sinai and in Canaan are never an anonymous crowd, but a collection of named tribes, each with its leaders, families, and heritage. This entry reminds the reader that even the smallest tribe of Israel is part of the great covenant that God made with Jacob; the very existence of the census of the Simeonites attests to God's providence and counting of His people.
